swap:4685720:QB:2577417:ACTIVE.text: ESPN wants Prescott in that spot, and FantasyPros' weekly projections put him ahead of Bryce Young too. Quarterback has been your weakest position all season, so take the free upgrade sitting on your own bench. The curse does not get a vote this week.

roster_ideas.text: Jason Myers is on a bye and nobody else on your roster kicks, so that slot scores nothing unless you claim someone. Evan McPherson is unowned in this league, per FantasyPros' ownership numbers, and he is the highest-projected kicker still available. Kickers are deeply boring right up until the week you do not have one.

roster_ideas.title: Offer Jayden Daniels to Cambri for Travis Etienne Jr. and Tucker Kraft
roster_ideas.text: You carry two quarterbacks and start one of them. Cambri has one, and he is doubtful. Running back has been your worst-producing position all season and she has backs to move, so the shapes fit. The pitch is short, she needs a quarterback, you need a back who scores, and you two do not play each other this week. Kraft is on a bye next week, so he helps you the week after. If she balks at Etienne, Zach Charbonnet is a fair fallback, and FantasyPros still lists Etienne questionable with a hamstring, so check him before you start him. Two rosters built wrong in opposite directions is the only kind of trade that ever gets accepted.

matchup:2:4567048:OUT.title: Next up: Amie, a back short
matchup:2:4567048:OUT.text: You draw Amie, and her highest-projected starter, Kenneth Walker III, is out with a groin injury per FantasyPros. She will have somebody else in that spot before kickoff, so trust Sunday's lineup over today's scouting report.

bye:-16026:DST:bye:none:none.text: Seattle and Cleveland both rest in Week 11, so owning two defenses this week is the same as owning none. The pickup below names a replacement.

advice_cards.text: FantasyPros' weekly projections put C.J. Stroud ahead of Trevor Lawrence at quarterback next week. Your receiver room is going to need every point the rest of the lineup can find, and this one is free.

roster_ideas.title: Add Wan'Dale Robinson at receiver
roster_ideas.text: Five of your receivers are out, on injured reserve, or questionable for next week. Wan'Dale Robinson is unowned in this league, per FantasyPros' ownership numbers, and FantasyPros projects him as the best receiver left on the wire from here to the end of the season. He is not Davante Adams, but he does have the advantage of playing.

matchup:7:4362628:ACTIVE.title: Next up: Samantha
matchup:7:4362628:ACTIVE.text: Samantha's highest-projected starter is Ja'Marr Chase, which is the least fun sentence on this page. You cannot do anything about him, so win it in the margins: fill the empty spots and start the healthy bodies.

out:4241478:FLEX:OUT:4702555:ACTIVE.text: ESPN lists Smith as out for Week 11. FantasyPros has him sidelined with a hamstring and still week to week, with no return date given. Jonah Coleman is healthy, has a game and is already on your bench. Move him into flex, the wild-card spot.

bye:4426502:WR:bye:4569618:ACTIVE.text: Atlanta is on a bye, so London is out of the picture next week. Garrett Wilson is healthy, playing, and already on your bench. One tap, no thinking required.

bye:-16014:DST:bye:none:none.text: Three Rams gone in one bye week. Nobody on your bench plays defense, so this needs a waiver claim. The pickup below names the best one available.

watch:4723820:QUESTIONABLE:15818:ACTIVE.text: Cooper played Sunday with an ankle injury, left early and did not draw a single target, per FantasyPros. advice_cards.text: FantasyPros' injury report lists Travis Etienne Jr. questionable with a hamstring, a week after he came off injured reserve and ran for very little against Carolina. ESPN has no designation on him at all. Two sources, two opinions, and only one of them has to be right on Sunday.

roster_ideas.title: Claim Tyler Shough at quarterback
roster_ideas.text: With Maye doubtful, your quarterback spot may be empty on Sunday, and that is the most expensive hole on a roster. Tyler Shough is unowned in this league, per FantasyPros' ownership numbers, and FantasyPros ranks him inside the top ten quarterbacks for next week. Free, available, and better than the alternative, which is nobody.

roster_ideas.title: Offer Travis Etienne Jr. and Tucker Kraft to Tara for Jayden Daniels
roster_ideas.text: You have five healthy running backs and no healthy quarterback. Tara carries two quarterbacks and starts one, and running back has been her worst-producing position all season, so a back and your second tight end for Jayden Daniels fixes a real hole on both rosters. Kraft is on a bye next week, so nothing you were going to start leaves the lineup. Say it plainly, and say that you do not play each other this week.

matchup:3:4241416:ACTIVE.title: Next up: Maddie
matchup:3:4241416:ACTIVE.text: Maddie is next, and the two of you are matched on record, so this is the most winnable game left on your board. Chuba Hubbard is the name to watch on her side. She also beat you to the Ravens defense this week, so there's a small score to settle.

out:4431452:QB:DOUBTFUL:none:none.text: Maye is doubtful for next week with an ankle injury, per ESPN. He is the only quarterback on your roster, so line up a waiver claim before kickoff in case he sits.

bye:4426385:RB:bye:3916148:ACTIVE.text: Seattle is on a bye, so Charbonnet sits out next week. Tony Pollard is healthy, playing, and the strongest back left on your bench. You started Pollard once before and it went rather well.

empty:WR:0:4426388:ACTIVE.text: There is nobody in one of your receiver slots, and an empty slot scores exactly nothing. Jameson Williams is healthy, playing, and sitting on your bench waiting to be asked.

summary.text: An empty receiver spot, a back on a bye, and a doubtful quarterback. All three fixes are below.

league.text: Six of eight lineups need a tap before kickoff, and ten starters are sitting out on byes. Marlee and Samantha are the only two with nothing to do. The bye weeks picked a fine time to gang up.

lineup:B:4431459:w5.title: Mostly right, one tight end regret
lineup:B:4431459:w5.text: You leave less on the bench than almost anyone. The exception is Week 5, when Harold Fannin started at tight end and Tyler Warren had a big one from your bench. You are being told to start Tyler Warren again in Week 11, so the universe is offering a redo.

pos:RB1:WR8.title: Best backfield, last-place receivers
pos:RB1:WR8.text: Your running backs lead the league and your receivers rank last, which is a strange way to keep winning. A.J. Brown and Drake London should not add up to last place.

proj:over:3915511:4870795.title: The gut was right about Burrow
proj:over:3915511:4870795.text: Your lineup has outrun its projections all season, with Joe Burrow the main reason and Makai Lemon the main drag. When your quarterback keeps beating his number, the move is to stop second-guessing him.

lineup:C:4685278:w7.title: Coker started, Burden scored
lineup:C:4685278:w7.text: Week 7 is the one to learn from: Jalen Coker started at receiver and did nothing while Luther Burden III had his best week of the season on your bench. You roster eight receivers and start three, so the odds of getting it wrong are baked in.

pos:TE2:K7.title: Brock Bowers is doing the heavy lifting
pos:TE2:K7.text: Tight end is your second-best position in the league and kicker your seventh, which is the least alarming weak spot available. Ka'imi Fairbairn is actually the best-projected kicker left this season, so this one may fix itself without you touching a thing.

proj:over:-16030:4695883.title: Your defense is outrunning its projection
proj:over:-16030:4695883.text: Your lineup finishes a shade ahead of its projections overall, carried by the Jaguars defense comfortably beating its number week after week. Jalen Coker has pulled the other way, which the Week 7 card above already covered.

lineup:B:4259545:w1.title: Nine weeks, one regret
lineup:B:4259545:w1.text: You squeeze about as much out of your roster as anyone in the league. The one that stings is Week 1, when Emeka Egbuka started in flex, the wild-card spot, and D'Andre Swift went off on your bench. Nine weeks on, Swift is still the one you are told to start, so the lesson landed.

pos:WR1:TE8.title: Best receivers, last-place tight end
pos:WR1:TE8.text: Your receivers lead the league and your tight end is dead last. You roster exactly one tight end. That is not a position group, it is a hope.

proj:over:4430878:4360248.title: Smith-Njigba keeps beating his number
proj:over:4430878:4360248.text: Your lineup has outscored its projections all season, led by Jaxon Smith-Njigba beating his number nearly every week. Kyle Pitts has gone the other way, which brings us back to tight end.

lineup:C:4360761:w8.title: Wilson's best week happened on your bench
lineup:C:4360761:w8.text: Your worst call this season was Week 8, when Tre Tucker blanked in your lineup and Michael Wilson had his best week of the year on your bench. Eight receivers on the roster, three slots, and the bench keeps picking the right ones.

pos:K2:WR7.title: Your kicker is carrying this team
pos:K2:WR7.text: Kicker is your second-best position in the league and wide receiver your seventh, which is a sentence nobody wants written about them. The fix is which ones start, not how many you keep.

proj:under:-16016:4360761.title: ESPN overrates everyone but your defense
proj:under:-16016:4360761.text: Your lineup has landed under ESPN's projections all season, with the Vikings defense the one piece quietly beating its number most weeks. Treat the projections as a suggestion.

lineup:C:4036378:w9.title: Week 9 was an expensive quarterback call
lineup:C:4036378:w9.text: Josh Allen started and had a quiet day while Jordan Love put up the biggest bench score anyone in this league has managed all season. You own two startable quarterbacks, so this decision comes back every single week. Worth five minutes on a Sunday morning.

pos:QB1:FLEX8.title: Six running backs and nothing to put in flex
pos:QB1:FLEX8.text: Quarterback is your strongest position in the league and flex, the wild-card spot, is your weakest, despite six running backs on the roster. Depth is not the problem. The top of it is.

proj:under:-16034:4429160.title: Under the number most weeks
proj:under:-16034:4429160.text: Your lineup lands under its projections most weeks. De'Von Achane was the biggest shortfall of the season while you held him, and the Texans defense has been the one beating its number. The trade below is aimed at it.

lineup:C:4248528:w1.title: Week 1 belonged to your bench
lineup:C:4248528:w1.text: Your biggest bench week was Week 1, when Christian Watson put up a monster game while your flex, the wild-card spot, barely scored. Watson has repaid the faith since, which is the actual lesson: your bench runs hot.

pos:TE1:RB7.title: Best tight end, thinnest backfield
pos:TE1:RB7.text: Trey McBride has made tight end your strongest position in the league, while running back sits seventh despite six of them on your roster. Six backs, seventh place.

proj:under:4248528:4569173.title: The projections miss you both ways
proj:under:4248528:4569173.text: Your lineup has come in under its projections most weeks, with Rhamondre Stevenson the steadiest drag and Christian Watson the one beating his number.

lineup:C:3916148:w7.title: Week 7 was the Pollard week
lineup:C:3916148:w7.text: Derrick Henry started at running back and did very little while Tony Pollard put up the biggest bench score on your roster all season. You started Pollard the next time it mattered and won, so this one is already filed under lesson learned.

pos:WR2:RB8.title: Last place in the backfield, with six of them
pos:WR2:RB8.text: Your receivers are second in the league and your running backs are last, despite six of them on the roster. Derrick Henry and Travis Etienne are the names on the shirt. Tony Pollard is the one scoring.

proj:over:4239993:4262921.title: Ahead of the projections, behind on the scoreboard
proj:over:4239993:4262921.text: Your lineup finishes slightly ahead of its projections, with Tee Higgins the biggest overachiever and Justin Jefferson coming up short more often than a player of his quality should. Nothing here is broken.

lineup:C:4241416:w1.title: Hubbard keeps scoring from the wrong side of the lineup
lineup:C:4241416:w1.text: Week 1 set the tone: Jaylen Waddle started in flex, the wild-card spot, and Chuba Hubbard outscored him many times over from your bench. Hubbard is still on this roster and still underused. Start the one who keeps scoring.

pos:K1:QB8.title: Your kicker leads the league
pos:K1:QB8.text: You have the best kicker in the league and the worst quarterback, which is a hard combination to build a season on. Quarterback is also the position where the wire most often has an upgrade.

proj:under:4241416:4047650.title: Nobody misses their number by more
proj:under:4241416:4047650.text: No lineup in the league has fallen further short of its projections than yours, with DK Metcalf the biggest weekly shortfall and Chuba Hubbard the one beating his. The roster is better than the results.
